{"basis":"measured","confidence":1.0,"fact_type":"defect","name":"MEASURED 2026-09-23: re-declaring an existing dependency with external_dependency REPLACES the Resource node and silently drops its `description` — a 3,015-character history on flo2's dep:reflow2 vanished","source":"who:claude-code, re-pinning flo2's dep:reflow2 from v0.66.0 to v0.67.0 with the v0.67.0 release binary; get_node before and after","statement":"WHAT WAS OBSERVED. flo2's `dep:reflow2` (a Resource, resource_type design-dependency) carried a 3,015-character `description`: the record of every earlier re-declaration and what each stale pin had cost. Re-declaring it at v0.67.0 with `external_dependency` (id, name, source, version, features, design_export, design_export_seen_at — no description, because the tool has no such parameter) returned success. Immediately afterwards `get_node` showed NO `description` property at all, and `replace_text` on it was refused naming the text properties the node now had, none of them `description`.

EXPECTED. Revising a node elsewhere in reflow2 keeps what the call omits — `add_resource`, `add_artifact` and the other constructors say so in their own descriptions ("omitted fields keep their stored value"). `external_dependency`'s description says a re-declare takes "a new baseline", which reads as moving the version and the watched export, not as discarding the node's prose.

NOT AFFECTED. `add_resource` on the same node with only `id` and `description` restored the text and kept every dependency field (version, features, design_export_hash) — so the node type holds both happily; it is the re-declare path that does not preserve.

IMPACT. The recurring job this tool exists for — re-pinning when upstream moves, which `loop_status` nags about on every release — erases whatever a project wrote about its dependency, with a success reply. flo2 caught it only because the next call targeted that field. Recovered here from the committed export; a project that re-exported first would have committed the loss. Not established: whether other properties outside the tool's parameter list are dropped the same way (only `description` was present to lose), or whether the revision guard's preserved-on-write snapshot captured the prior state.

SAME TOOL, SECOND LOSSY SHAPE — MEASURED 2026-09-24 on flo2's move to v0.70.0: `external_dependency` stores `features` as ONE comma-joined string, so a feature whose text contains a comma comes back as several. "the jot skill: /jot, /note and /log-issue, the word is the tag (0.70.0)" was stored and echoed as three features ("the jot skill: /jot", "/note and /log-issue", "the word is the tag (0.70.0)"), and the dependency manifest the call returns shows the split. Worked around by re-declaring with a comma-free wording. Nothing refuses or warns; a caller only sees it by reading the echoed manifest. Found from the dev_reflow2 hub session.","steps":["external_dependency"],"subject_id":"cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported","valid_from":"2026-09-23"}
